quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What can goggles do?

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Give you an escape route.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Protects only your eyes.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up rather than to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to balance in turns. Use your arms for steering, not for holding yourself up. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Before riding, your pre-ride check should include all of the following, except:

options.text: Checking your tires.
Testing your taillight.
Testing your headlight.
Checking your paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your paint.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do not need to check your paint.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than 5 miles, within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of the stopping power

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the road is wet.
Only sometimes.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow or stop to get the most stopping power.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Not use space cushions.
Increase their space cushions.
Reduce their space cushions by half.
Keep adequate space cushions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider to be safe.

questions.question: Which of the following do you NOT need to check before riding?

options.text: Your tire pressure.
The tread on your tires.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread wear, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best protection for your face?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you first. For example, when a corner is on your right, move to the left side of your lane so drivers see you sooner.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, what formation should a group use?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is normally best for group riding. However, switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is worse than riding behind the vehicle.
It limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during daylight.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Never ride directly beside another vehicle. The driver may not see you, and they could turn into your lane. Also, the vehicle will block your escape route if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What causes most motorcycle and car crashes at intersections?

options.text: Drivers not properly yielding to motorcycles.
Riders not seeing cars entering from side streets.
Drivers tailgating riders.
Riders not yielding to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers not properly yielding to motorcycles.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to properly yield the right-of-way to riders. Always be alert when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually will not hear a tire fail.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until it loses interest.
Swerve around it.
Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When going faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn will make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car crashes happen because:

options.text: A driver pulls into a motorcycle's path.
They result in minor injuries.
A motorcyclist turns left in front of a car.
Of speeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver pulls into a motorcycle's path.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by drivers failing to properly yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists.
